labels.text: [ENTER to send, 'e' to edit, 'r' to re-record, ESC to discard]

S110.07.note: The voice loop sends the transcript through the same session.send call as typed text (apps/cli/src/voice.rs). No task creation or Tasks step was found in voice.rs, so the durable background task part is not confirmed by code.
steps: Type /voice and press Enter.
Press SPACE to start recording, say the request, then stop recording as the prompt shows.
Press ENTER to send the transcribed text (or e to edit it first).
Look at the chat: the request should be sent to the agent. Compare with Expected: it should become a background task that shows in Tasks.

S110.08.note: The voice send path is the same as typed input (apps/cli/src/voice.rs, session.send). No voice-specific document output or open control was found. Searched apps/cli/src/voice.rs, apps/cli/src/documents.rs and all of apps/cli/src for docx and pdf references; the document result depends on what the agent produces, which this code audit did not confirm.

labels.text: Save the task you just finished as a reusable skill

S110.14.note: The command sends a prompt that asks the agent to write .agiworkforce/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs, save_skill_prompt). Whether the skill then appears in the Skills list was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Finish a normal task in agi.
Type /save-skill and press Enter, optionally with a name after it.
Wait for the agent to write the skill file and show it to you.
Check that the file exists at .agiworkforce/skills/<name>/SKILL.md in the project folder, then start a new task that needs it and see whether the skill is used. Compare with Expected.
S110.14.where: /save-skill typed after a task finishes (optionally followed by a name)

labels.text: Turn the task you just finished into a scheduled routine

S110.15.note: /save-routine only sends a prompt that makes the agent call cron_create (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs, save_routine_prompt). It does not run the cloud admit check that /schedule uses. The step 3 tool name is cron_create, not cron_check: correct it when following this. Whether the scheduled run succeeds is not shown in code.
steps: Finish a normal task in agi.
Type /save-routine and press Enter, adding how often it should run, or leave it blank and answer the agent's question.
Wait for the agent to create the routine with cron_check tool and state the schedule and what each run does.
Wait for the first scheduled run and check that it did the same work and finished successfully. Compare with Expected.
S110.15.where: /save-routine typed after a task finishes (optionally followed by how often it runs)

S110.19.needs: a Desktop app and a CLI session in the same folder
S110.19.note: CLI sessions are stored with the source value cli in apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs (source_to_stored). The desktop app's local-sessions list and folder filter are not in apps/cli, and the cited lib.rs line moved. The CLI side starts with agi resume (apps/cli/src/lib.rs, Continue previous session). The desktop screen words were not found in apps/cli.

labels.text: Continue a local session in a new cloud Code session

S110.22.needs: a signed-in account, a git repository with a pushed branch, a local session in that folder
S110.22.note: The cited lib.rs:2774 moved. The handoff command is the Handoff variant of CodeSubcommand (apps/cli/src/lib.rs). handle_code_handoff refuses with an unpushed-commit message (apps/cli/src/lib.rs) because the cloud session clones the pushed branch.
steps: Push any unpushed commits: the handoff refuses while commits are not pushed.
In the repository folder, type agi code handoff and press Enter, optionally with a local session id.
Read the review shown and answer the prompt to continue, or use -y to skip the prompt.
Open the cloud session link printed at the end and check that the history and pending work came with it. Compare with Expected.
S110.22.where: agi code handoff typed in the repository folder

labels.text: Link this directory to an account project by id or name.

S110.24.needs: a signed-in account with an account project
S110.24.note: The CLI has no in-chat picker for a notebook or project. The link is made in the shell, and the word notebook is not used in apps/cli. Grounding is in apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs (project_conversation).
steps: Sign in to the account and make sure the privacy mode is Managed (project knowledge is used only in Managed mode).
In the folder, type agi projects link followed by the project name or id.
Start agi in that folder and ask a question that the project's instructions or files should answer.
Compare the answer with the project's instructions and sources. If a notice says the turn runs without your project's knowledge files, the link did not take effect.
S110.24.where: agi projects link <project> typed in the shell, then agi started in the same folder

labels.text: Run `agi usage` to see when it resets.
Add credits or fix billing at

S110.26.needs: a Free account or a paid account at its usage limit
S110.26.note: The named alternative appears only when a cached model list has a model other than the limited one (apps/cli/src/errors.rs, plan_alternative). The purchase link appears only for the billing recovery path. The one-step switch uses the /model text shown in the error.
steps: Use the account until its usage limit is reached (a test account at its limit is easiest).
In agi, send any message.
Read the error: it gives a reset time, and if a model is listed it says Your plan also includes that model. It can also show a billing or plans link.
Type /model with the named model, send the message again, and check that the chat continues. Compare with Expected.
S110.26.where: agi, any chat message sent after the usage limit is reached; read the error text
